metadata.title: Average of Levels in Binary Tree

problem_summary.summary: Compute the arithmetic mean of the node values at each tree level, from top to bottom.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: the root of a non-empty binary tree. Return one double average per level; answers within 10^-5 of the exact values are accepted.

brute_force.explanation: Use an explicit depth-first stack carrying each node's depth, and accumulate a sum and count for every depth. Convert each pair to an average afterward.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every node is visited exactly once with its actual depth, so each depth's sum and count include exactly its level's nodes. Dividing that sum by its count yields the required average.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — each node is visited once, followed by one pass over the levels.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary in the worst case for the explicit DFS stack and per-level sums/counts; the returned list has O(h) values.

optimized.explanation: Use breadth-first search, snapshot the queue size at the start of each level, and compute that level's sum while removing exactly those nodes.
optimized.correctness_idea: At the start of an iteration, the queue contains exactly one level. Processing its fixed initial size prevents newly enqueued children from entering the current sum, so each average uses exactly the nodes of one level.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — every node is enqueued and processed once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(w) auxiliary for the queue, where w is the maximum level width; the returned list has O(h) values.

steps.condition: The root is the only node in this level.
steps.action: Divide the level sum 8 by its node count 1.

steps.condition: The queue size captured at level start is 2; children are deferred to the next level.
All three remaining nodes belong to this level.
steps.action: Compute 30 / 3 and finish when the queue is empty.

edge_cases.handling: Its average is the node value itself.
The signed sum is divided as a double, preserving a negative or fractional mean.

edge_cases.case: Large positive or negative values on one level
edge_cases.handling: A long accumulator prevents overflow when adding up to 10^4 integer node values.
